To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have experimentally validated the majority of the GENCODE annotated transcript structures and that we have identified a large number of novel exons and genes in the human genome.

We combined targeted and unbiased approaches, RT PCR seq and HBM RNA seq, to catalog all protein coding genes and pseudogenes in the human genome, and discovered a large number of novel noncoding transcripts.

1) RT PCR seq is a powerful tool to validate the accuracy of the GENCODE annotations, 2) RT PCR seq can be used to validate the accuracy and sensitivity of RNA sequencing experiments, 3) RT PCR seq has been used to validate 1168 novel gene models predicted by the Human Body Map RNA sequencing data, 4) RT PCR seq identified unannotated exonic regions in 11% of assessed human genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the annotation of the entire set of human genes, including their transcriptional start sites, splice junctions and polyadenylation sites, as well as the identification of noncoding RNAs, pseudogenes and antisense transcripts.
cataloging the genic elements in the human genome, and the methods we have developed will be useful in the annotation of the genomes of other species as well.
the identification of all protein coding genes and pseudogenes in the human genome and with the characterization of the non protein coding transcripts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GENCODE is the best annotated gene set to date and will be further improved as the ENCODE project continues.
GENCODE is an extremely valuable resource, which will be continuously improved and refined as the field moves forward.
the GENCODE project has provided a high quality annotation of all protein coding and non coding transcripts encoded in the human reference genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RT PCR seq data set, in combination with RNA seq, has provided a significant boost in the accuracy of the GENCODE annotation, which will continue to be updated as new data becomes available.
the GENCODE annotation is a high quality catalog of the human genic elements.

RT PCR seq is a very powerful tool to validate the accuracy of gene annotations, especially when used in conjunction with RNA seq data, which has the advantage of detecting novel transcripts, but not necessarily the novel exons within known genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RT PCR seq is a powerful tool to complement RNA seq and other transcriptome profiling methods, and it should be used in concert with them to annotate and validate the human genome.
the GENCODE gene catalog is of high quality and that the GENCODE annotation will be a valuable reference for future studies of the human transcriptome.
the GENCODE gene models are highly accurate, and that RT PCR seq is a powerful and efficient tool for experimental validation of predicted transcripts, which will complement the GENCODE gene catalog.
